newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada raises bank rate 25 bps to 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada raises bank rate 25 bps to 3.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Canada raised its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent by intervening in the money market on Thursday.

The move effectively raised the central bank's target range for the call loan or overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.5 from 2.75-3.25 percent. The bank rate is the top of the central bank's target range for the overnight rate, and is also the rate at which it lends to financial institutions in its role as lender of last resort. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.
The central bank said in a statement following the move that the rate hike was designed to "counter excessive easing in monetary conditions and to provide support for the currency."
In May, the central bank said publicly that the need for further easing had largely disappeared. However, since then the Canadian dollar has weakened sharply, further easing monetary conditions.
In today's release the Bank said recent economic information had reinforced the view that the need for easing had disappeared.

The Bank of Canada last year brought the bank rate to its lowest level since December, 1961, after lowering short-term rates 11 times. Ten of those rate reductions were independent of rate cuts by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
